_comment: check-citations.py config. A pin is [citing doc, cited path, regex the cited line must match, what it is evidence of, and — when the doc cites that path more than once — an ANCHOR regex matching prose within 2 lines of the ONE citation the claim is about. Without the anchor a pin over a multiply-cited path checks the SET of cited lines, not the sentence; the gate now refuses such a pin instead of passing it. Add a pin whenever a doc cites a line as proof that a rule is enforced.
_scanned: No 'scanned' key on purpose: this file used to copy the defaults verbatim, which froze the scan at seven root-level files and missed docs/ and specs/ entirely — the run reported 'Checked 0 citation(s) ... PASS'. Omitting the key follows plugins/loopkit/scripts/check-citations.py's DEFAULT_SCANNED, which now covers docs/**, specs/** and the plugin's own agents and skills.
_allow_empty: false since 2026-09-07. It was true while no document in this repo cited a file:line; both docs/GETTING-STARTED.md and specs/blocked-waits-on-what.md now do, so an EMPTY scan from here means the scan lost the docs, and that is red.
pins: the citation gate is actually invoked against this repo, with no --root
CI reaches that gate by running the suite
the queue is exactly five columns, which is why the spec forbids a sixth and puts the condition in the `spec` cell
the read-side rewrite the condition grammar must survive (collapses whitespace runs)
the write-side rewrite the condition grammar must survive (escapes literal pipes)
the closed four/five-column header list; a six-column header matches neither, which is why the spec forbids a sixth column
the cell-count mismatch that records a dropped row; paired with the short-read invariant below it is a refusal, no longer a silent skip
`blocked` is absent from WANT, so a blocked row is counted and never served
scope matching hays finding+source, which is why the condition may not live in either
the control case's absolute-path scrubbing already exists here and should be extended, not rewritten
update_row leaves the spec cell untouched when the argument is None, which is why criterion 10 cannot rely on the caller remembering to clear a spent condition
no recognisable header, but the file holds
the refusal that replaced the silent zero — the spec's old 'rows parsed: 0, exit 0' argument for the no-sixth-column SHALL is dead, and the SHALL now rests on cross-version compatibility instead
the short-read invariant: a row that fails the cell-count check is refused, not silently deleted, which is why the grammar table reads PARSE REFUSED
^    header = "\| finding \| source \| priority \| spec \| status \|"$
write_table hardcodes the five-column header, so a sixth column cannot round-trip even if a parser admitted it
the single reader of ACCEPTED_HEADERS, so a six-column header is rejected in exactly one place
_as_of: specs/blocked-waits-on-what.md writes its citations as `path:line as of <sha>`. check-citations.py matches path:line and ignores the suffix, so the convention is free to the gate and still checked by it.
